Article Title: 'Prioritise national interest': Shashi Tharoor advises govt to keep Brics 'non-West'
Article Text:
Shashi Tharoor says govt must keep Brics non-West and not let it appear anti-West.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Shashi Tharoor on Friday cautioned that the Brics summit hosted by India should not appear to be an anti-West platform, as that would not be in sync with the country’s national interests.Tharoor, who served as a diplomat at the United Nations for decades, advised the government to showcase the concerns of the Global South while keeping India’s direct national interests in mind."As chair, we have a particular responsibility to showcase both the Brics as a forum, the concerns of the Global South in general, but also while bearing very, very carefully in mind our direct national interests. We want Brics to be a forum that is non-West, but not anti-West. That is exactly actually the same agenda as every other country. There are some others in Brics who are very happy to take it as a geopolitical non-Western, but also anti-Western platform," Tharoor told news agency PTI.He also said that PM Modi's scheduled meeting with Chinese president Xi Jinping and the meeting with Russian president Vladimir Putin "are going to grab world headlines"."And I would like to say that that would not be in India's national interest...Becauseall these world leaders are in India, there will be significant bilateral conversations. Our Prime Minister is bound to be meeting each of the visiting heads of state and government who seeks a meeting. And that may mean a dozen important meetings with these country leaders. And for us, of course, both the meeting with President Xi and the meeting with President Putin are going to grab world headlines," the Thiruvananthapuram Lok Sabha MP said.Former Union minister Salman Khurshid also described the gathering as a “significant event” that allows India to demonstrate leadership on the global stage.Speaking to ANI, Khurshid stressed that the presence of leaders from all 11 member countries, including China, Iran, Russia, South Africa and India, could help New Delhi bring countries together, reduce contradictions and conflicts, and work towards creating better conditions in the world."This is a significant event. We hosted the G20 summit a few years ago, and the important thing is that the top leadership of China, Iran, Russia, South Africa, and India will all be present. All 11 countries will be present. It allows India to demonstrate leadership and ensure that contradictions and conflicts are reduced to a minimum. It can't be done overnight, but at least some attempt should be made. For India to have a locus as the leader and chairperson of the Brics summit, to be able to bring people together, converge, and accept positions that will create better conditions in the world," he said.Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday said leaders from across the world would gather in New Delhi over the next few days for the Brics summit, expressing confidence that the high-level meeting would see positive and meaningful discussions on various issues with the welfare of the world in mind.“Over the next few days, leaders from around the world will gather for the Brics Summit. I am confident that the Summit will see positive and meaningful discussions on various issues with the welfare of the world in mind,” Modi said in a post on X in Hindi.The Prime Minister also shared a Sanskrit shlok highlighting the importance of cultivating relationships with virtuous people and promoting dialogue and goodwill.“A person should always live among the virtuous and cultivate their company. A person should engage in discussion and foster friendly relations with the virtuous, because mutual goodwill, dialogue and friendly relations strengthen peace and cooperation,” the verse said in a loose translation.As Brics chair in 2026, India will host the 18th Brics summit in New Delhi on September 12 and 13. The summit will bring together leaders of Brics member and partner countries, as well as outreach invitees.During the summit, leaders are expected to discuss ways to strengthen intra-Brics cooperation on common priorities and exchange views on global and regional issues of mutual importance, according to a statement issued by the Ministry of External Affairs.Earlier on Thursday night, Bharat Mandapam, the venue for the summit in New Delhi, was being readied to host the high-profile gathering, with leaders and representatives from across the world expected to arrive for the September 12-13 event.
Article Summary: Shashi tharoor says govt must keep brics non-west and not let it appear anti-west. He also said that pm modi's scheduled meeting with chinese president xi jinping and the meeting with russian president vladimir putin "are going to grab world headlines" the summit will bring together leaders of brics member and partner countries, as well as outreach invitees.

Article Title: Brics Summit 2026: Putin to land in Delhi in few hours; Xi arriving Saturday - top developments
Article Text:
India is set to host the two-day BRICS summit in New Delhi, bringing together global leaders while showcasing the country’s cultural heritage.

Key leaders in India

Key agenda, topics in focus

'All set': PM Modi

Schedule

1,200-1,300 journalists expected

Cultural showcase

Delhi all decked up with beefed up security

India chairs Brics for the fourth time

NEW DELHI: Russian foreign minister Sergey Lavrov arrived in India ahead of the BRICS Summit 2026.Russian President Vladimir Putin is also scheduled to arrive in India later tonight.The 18th Brics Leaders’ Summit will be held in New Delhi on September 12-13, bringing together leaders of the expanded grouping for discussions on economic cooperation, technology, energy and food security, global governance and major geopolitical issues. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will host the summit at Bharat Mandapam as India concludes its year-long Brics chairship and hold key meetings with Putin, Xi jinping and various other leaders.The summit comes amid looming concerns over Russia-Ukraine war, Middle East crisis, Strait of Hormuz shipping and continuing global trade tensions. Leaders are expected to work towards a New Delhi Declaration, while the two-day programme will also include bilateral meetings, an exhibition visit, a gala dinner and cultural events.Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, South African President Cyril Ramaphosa and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto are among the key leaders expected in New Delhi.UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres will also attend. PM Modi is scheduled to hold bilateral meetings with several leaders on the sidelines of the summit. His meeting with Putin on Friday comes after their recent talks at the SCO summit, while his engagement with Pezeshkian will take place against the backdrop of the Middle East conflict. The Russian president is set to reach in just a few hours with expected time of arrival 1.15am on September 11.The Prime Minister is scheduled to hold bilateral talks with Putin at 3.30 pm and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian at 6.15 pm on Friday. Then, according to sources cited by PTI, PM's meeting with Xi Jinping is scheduled for 6 pm on Saturday. During the Modi-Xi talks, the two leaders are expected to review the situation along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) and discuss further steps to normalise bilateral ties, including expanding trade and investment, people familiar with the matter said.The China leader is scheduled to reach Infdia at 12.25 pm on Saturday, September 12.Also read: Putin meeting PM Modi on Friday; energy, defence high on agenda Xi’s visit is particularly significant as it will be his first trip to India in seven years. The Chinese president is expected to travel with a large delegation, with sources, cited by Reuers, earlier estimating around 400 officials, more than twice the number that accompanied him in 2019. His visit comes as New Delhi and Beijing work to stabilise ties after years of border tensions.Read more: China confirms Xi Jinping's India visit for Brics summit on September 12-13, first trip in 7 years Meanwhile, foreign ministers of Ethiopia and Burundi, Gedion Timothewos and Edouard Bizimana, have already arrived in New Delhi on Thursday. Later, Brazil minister of foreign affairs Mauro Vieira also reached New Delhi. Country's president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will not be coming due to upcoming Brazil elections.Food and energy security, healthcare, disaster resilience and critical supply chains will be among the key areas of discussion.Leaders are also expected to discuss trade, investment, connectivity, cross-border payments, greater use of national currencies, MSME development, digital trade and artificial intelligence.Development finance, climate resilience, expansion of the New Development Bank and reforms of multilateral financial and political institutions are also on the agenda.The Russia-Ukraine war, the Middle East war and concerns over the Strait of Hormuz are expected to feature in discussions on global and regional developments.US tariff policies and wider changes in global trade will provide the broader economic backdrop. Since Brics decisions are consensus-based, differences among members could make negotiations on the joint declaration challenging.New Delhi is gearing up for the two-day summit, with Bharat Mandapam decked up to welcome world leaders.Modi shared a video of the venue on X on Thursday, ending with the message, “India is gearing up for BRICS 2026”. Sharing the video, he wrote: “All set for BRICS 2026!”The video contains visuals of the Bharat Mandapam, the sprawling complex in central Delhi, which has been decked up for the Summit that is being held on September 12-13 under India's chairship.India is hosting the 18th Brics Summit as the grouping's 2026 chair, with leaders of member and partner countries as well as outreach invitees expected to participate.The main leaders’ programme begins on Saturday, September 12.At 2.35 pm, Brics member-country leaders will hold a closed-door session on “Inclusive Global Governance and Strengthening Multilateralism”. At 4.25 pm, leaders will tour the Bharat Innovates Exhibition, followed by a family photograph and joint tree-planting ceremony at 5.05 pm.PM Modi will host a gala dinner at 7.30 pm.Then, on Sunday, September 13, leaders of member countries, partner nations and outreach invitees will begin arriving at 9:55 am. The official group photograph is scheduled for 10.35 am, followed by the main open session at 10:50 am, titled “Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability: Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth”.The summit is expected to conclude with the New Delhi Declaration.The ministry of external affairs expects around 1,200-1,300 journalists to cover the summit, with Indian and foreign media expected to be roughly evenly represented.An International Media Centre is being set up at Bharat Mandapam. The government plans to disseminate information through press releases, websites and social media platforms linked to India’s Brics presidency.Around 160 artistes from India and other Brics countries will perform the “Brics Symphony” at PM Modi’s gala dinner on September 12. The programme will feature Bharatanatyam, Kuchipudi, Odissi and Kathak, along with traditional instruments and vocal performances.A special Brics Friendship Mural is also being created at Bharat Mandapam by artists from member countries, inspired by “Sangam”, or confluence.BRICS banners and posters have gone up across the New Delhi district, while prominent areas including Connaught Place and Khan Market have seen enhanced lighting at night. Security agencies have also stepped up surveillance, with around 500 CCTV cameras deployed across the area, including some equipped with number plate recognition technology.Manish Kumar Agrawal, Special Commissioner of Police (Protective/Security Division), said, "We have made elaborate bandobast by ensuring minimum inconvenience to the public. We have also issued advance advisories regarding traffic arrangements," Agrawal said.Delhi Police has put in place multi-layered security and quick-response arrangements to ensure the movement of visiting leaders and delegates. Senior officers have also been directed to maintain strict vigilance and ensure smooth coordination during the summit.Traffic restrictions are expected in parts of the city during the movement of foreign dignitaries, which could affect commuters despite markets and commercial areas remaining operational.Also read: Going to airport, central Delhi or south Delhi? BRICS traffic restrictions you need to know Connaught Place will remain open from September 11 to 13, although traffic restrictions linked to the summit may affect movement.The Delhi Metro Museum at Supreme Court Metro station will remain closed from September 11 to 13 and reopen on September 15.Rashtrapati Bhavan, the Rashtrapati Bhavan Museum and Amrit Udyan will also remain closed to the public from September 11 to 13. The Change of Guard ceremony scheduled for September 12 will not take place.Also read: Brics Summit, nationwide bank strike tomorrow: Are banks open or shut on September 11? Check details Northern Railway has also made temporary changes to train operations from September 11 to 13. Several trains from New Delhi and nearby stations have been cancelled, diverted, rescheduled or short-terminated/originated during the period. Passengers have been advised to check the National Train Enquiry System (NTES) or call 139 for the latest updates before travelling.Read more: Operations at New Delhi railway station to be regulated; several trains cancelled, diverted - check full list Meanwhile, Delhi is likely to witness rain on both days, with the IMD forecasting light to moderate rainfall in parts of the city, even as temperatures remained above normal on Thursday.India assumed the Brics chairship on January 1, 2026, for the fourth time, after previous chairships in 2012, 2016 and 2021.India’s theme for the year is “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability”, with “Humanity First” as its people-centric approach. During its chairship, India has held more than 350 meetings and high-level engagements across more than 25 cities.Brics originally comprised Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa. Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, the UAE and Saudi Arabia joined in 2024, while Indonesia became a member in 2025.Ten countries, including Belarus, Bolivia, Kazakhstan, Cuba, Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand, Uganda, Uzbekistan and Vietnam, have joined as partner countries.The 11-member grouping accounts for about 49.5 per cent of the world's population, around 40 per cent of global GDP and about 26 per cent of global trade, according to Indian government figures.
Article Summary: The 18th brics leaders’ summit will be held in new delhi on september 12-13. The two-day programme will also include bilateral meetings, an exhibition visit, a gala dinner and cultural events. Russian president vladimir putin, chinese president xi jinping, iranian president masoud pezeshkian, south african president cyril ramaphosa and indonesian president prabowo subianto are among the key leaders expected to attend.

Article Title: Modi-Xi meet: Trade, border on agenda during Xi's 24-hour blitz
Article Text:
Xi Jinping to visit India after 7 years, attend BRICS Summit on Sept 12-13

China announced Thursday President Xi Jinping ’s first visit to India in 7 years, saying he will attend the Brics summit in New Delhi from September 12 to 13 at the invitation of PM Narendra Modi. His bilateral with Modi is scheduled for Saturday evening, according to diplomatic sources.TOI has learnt that Xi will be accompanied by a 67-member government delegation, including political heavyweight and Xi’s right-hand man Cai Qi - member of the standing committee of the CPC Politburo - and foreign minister Wang Yi. A business delegation is arriving separately for the president’s visit that will last exactly for 24 hours, beginning with Xi’s arrival at 12.10 pm on Saturday and 12.20 pm departure the next day.Xi will arrive at Bharat Mandapam around 2 pm on Saturday, where he and other leaders will be welcomed by Modi. The bilateral meeting between the leaders is likely to take place between the Brics closed session on multilateralism and the dinner that Modi will host for the leaders at 7.30 pm in which Xi will also be present.There has been speculation about why Beijing delayed the announcement of the visit, but it’s learnt that China had formally conveyed to the Indian side Xi’s participation weeks earlier.On August 27, China officially requested the Indian embassy in Beijing to issue visas to the president’s delegation.Xi’s visit is expected to reinforce the positive momentum in bilateral ties since the meeting between the leaders on the margins of the BRICS summit in Kazan in 2024, which marked complete disengagement and resolution of issues related to the 2020 eastern Ladakh military standoff. Modi is expected to underline India’s concerns about fair market access, supply chain reliability and balance in bilateral trade in the meeting, as the 2 sides look to boost economic cooperation.The leaders had in Kazan agreed to restart high-level engagements, calling upon Special Representatives on the India-China boundary question to oversee the management of peace and tranquility in border areas, which India calls a prerequisite for overall development of ties, and to explore a fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable solution to the boundary question. They also agreed to maintain contact at the level of foreign minister and other senior officials.Since then, the special representatives have thrice held boundary talks, with the latest meeting in August this year resulting in 8 outcomes that included a decision to finalise terms of reference for an early and substantial harvest of boundary delimitation and border management.Modi last year also visited China for the SCO summit, during which he also had a bilateral meeting with Xi. That visit too further solidified the thaw in ties, with both leaders agreeing that India and China are partners, not rivals. Xi’s visit is important for Beijing also as China assumes BRICS presidency next year, succeeding India’s chairship. The president had not travelled to Brazil last year for the BRICS summit.During his visit to Tianjin, Modi had also met Cai and shared his vision for bilateral relations and seeking his support to realise the vision of the two leaders. According to the Indian government, Cai had reiterated the Chinese sides desire to expand bilateral exchanges and further improve relations in line with the consensus reached between the two leaders.
Article Summary: Xi jinping to visit india after 7 years, attend brics summit on sept 12-13. His bilateral with modi is scheduled for saturday evening, according to diplomatic sources. Xi’s visit is important for beijing also as china assumes brics presidency next year.

Article Title: Russia President Vladimir Putin arrives in India ahead of Brics Summit 2026, to meet PM Modi
Article Text:
PM Modi to meet Putin later in the day

NEW DELHI: Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in India on early Friday ahead of the Brics Summit 2026.Russian president's official air vehicle landed at Delhi airport.During his visit, Putin is scheduled to hold talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and participate in a series of bilateral meetings.This mark his first overseas participation in a Brics Summit since Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022.The two leaders are expected to discuss the full range of India-Russia ties, with trade, energy and defence cooperation likely to figure prominently.The visit comes just days after PM Modi and Putin met on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek on August 31. At that meeting, the two leaders reviewed cooperation in areas including political ties, trade, defence, energy, space and mobility, while also discussing the conflicts in West Asia and the Black Sea region.Putin’s presence in Delhi also comes as India and Russia seek to deepen economic engagement despite mounting geopolitical pressure over Moscow’s war in Ukraine and Western restrictions on Russian trade.Russian presidential spokesperson Dmitry Peskov had earlier said the two sides are also exploring cooperation in rare earths, along with the possible sale of Sukhoi Su-57 stealth fighter jets to India.Speaking to reporters during a virtual briefing from Moscow, Peskov said, "We're looking forward to the President and Prime Minister having another bilateral meeting during the visit.It is scheduled. It is scheduled for Friday, so first, like always, they will touch on the bilateral agenda. Trade and economic cooperation is a very wide scope."On the agenda during Putin’s visit for the summit is also the possible sale of Russia’s Su-57 stealth fighters to India.Union civil aviation minister Kinjarapu Ram Mohan Naidu confirmed on Thursday that India and Russia have stepped up talks on manufacturing aircraft in India, including the IL-114 turboprop and Sukhoi Superjet 100.
Article Summary: Russian president vladimir putin arrives in india ahead of the brics summit 2026. Putin is scheduled to hold talks with prime minister narendra modi and participate in a series of bilateral meetings. Pm modi to meet putin later in the day in delhi.

Article Title: BSP's family drama: Why no 'Anand' for Mayawati ahead of Uttar Pradesh elections?
Article Text:
Mayawati said Akash Anand, the BSP's national coordinator, would continue to work in the party. (File Photo)

FIL bends but Mayawati refuses to budge

Akash Anand's on-off jouney with BSP.

Third time unlucky?

Anand's FIL connection and maturity question

Can BSP afford this 'family drama'?

NEW DELHI: Three promotions. Three demotions. And now staring at a possible exit!Well, that’s how the political scorecard reads for Akash Anand, whose “maturity meter” has not just failed him again, but has also put him on the brink of exit from the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP).7 days after his third demotion, Akash Anand finds himself in a difficult spot, with BSP chief Mayawati opening the doors for his exit from the party. "The people in the party feel that just as he was relieved of all the important responsibilities of the post of national coordinator on September 3, 2026, he should now also be completely freed from the party from today. Therefore, if Akash Anand wants to remain independent in the party, he is free to do so; that is, he has now been completely freed from the party," Mayawati posted on X.This despite the fact that Akash Anand's father-in-law, former Rajya Sabha MP Ashok Siddharth on Thursday bowed before Mayawati's ultimatum and announced his retirement from politics and social life, after the BSP chief linked his "sanyas" to any future reinstatement of responsibilities to her nephew Akash Anand.In an emotional post on X, Siddharth said he was retiring from political and social life "right now", adding that if he ever had to give his life for Mayawati, it would be a matter of pride for him.But neither Siddharth's actions nor his words made any impact on Mayawati.She questioned Siddharth's intentions, saying his "announcement should have come immediately after her call for him to retire." Mayawati alleged that the delay showed that Siddharth's ambitions and intentions had not changed completely."If Ashok Siddharth had even a little genuine concern for the bright future of his son-in-law Akash Anand and the larger interests of the BSP and its Ambedkarite Bahujan movement, he would have announced his retirement without delay," she said.Mayawati also slammed Anand for not reposting her earlier X post linking his future responsibilities in the party to his father-in-law's retirement. She said Anand had earlier reposted posts from her social media account "to demonstrate his loyalty," but had not done so in this case despite the post being in his own interest.Mayawati said this indicated that both Siddharth and Anand were more attached to personal and family interests than to the success of the party and its movement.She questioned whether Anand could effectively serve the BSP while remaining caught between his family ties and the interests of the party."If Akash Anand is less concerned about the real interests of the party and the movement and his own political career, and more attached to family relationships, then it is natural to ask how he can work for the good of the BSP and the movement while remaining double-minded," she said.Akash Anand’s latest demotion was on September 3, when aunt Mayawati announced that her nephew had again lost his political maturity."I have allowed Akash Anand to work in the party, which is before all of you, but Akash Anand still needs to become more mature. Till then, it would not be appropriate to give him a major responsibility in the party," Mayawati said at a national-level meeting of BSP office-bearers.And that ensured Akash Anand, the chief national coordinator of BSP, was back to square one. His Twitter bio reflected the sudden change in his status within the party. From BSP "National Convenor", he became "Party Worker, BSP." Just a few days later, he made yet another edit to his bio, which read: "Party Supporter, BSP." This is how his X bio reads now.It was less than a month back, August 10 to be exact, that Akash Anand had formally launched the BSP’s election campaign for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections from Sadabad assembly constituency in Hathras. He addressed a well-attended rally and launched a broadside against the BJP government in Uttar Pradesh over jobs, education and law and order, while taking digs at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, calling them both “uncle. ”From being anointed Mayawati’s successor to being a party worker and now a party supporter - it has been a tumultuous and bumpy ride for the young Akash Anand. And this time around there is a twist in the tale: Akash’s younger brother Ishan Anand has been brought to the centre stage.On September 3, when Mayawati entered the venue of the meeting of office-bearers, walking behind her was not Akash but his younger brother Ishan. Wearing the BSP's blue sash around his neck, he stood behind his aunt till she settled down.Akash Anand entered politics in 2017 at the young age of 22. Anand, who did his MBA from London, made his political debut with Mayawati at a rally in Uttar Pradesh's Saharanpur, where he shared the dais with Akhilesh Yadav and Ajit Singh.In April 2019, Akash Anand addressed his first rally in Uttar Pradesh's Agra. The BSP was then part of the opposition Mahagathbandhan, an anti-Congress and anti-BJP bloc formed in the run-up to the 2019 general election under the leadership of Akhilesh Yadav and Mayawati with Ajit Singh's Rashtriya Lok Dal.Mayawati appointed him BSP’s national coordinator in June 2019. Since then, it has been a bumpy ride for him. Every promotion since then has been followed by a demotion.After 6 days of suspense, Mayawati finally revealed what triggered her against Akash Anand yet again. In a long post on X, Mayawati explained how Akash Anand had once again, after two years, lost his “political maturity.” And also, what he could do to get it back.The trigger this time around was Ashok Siddharth, the father in law of Akash Anand. Ashok Siddharth was expelled by Maywati from BSP last month for the second time over indiscipline and anti-party stance.Taking to X, the BSP supremo wrote: “It is well known that Ashok Siddharth had previously been expelled for indiscipline and violating guidelines, specifically regarding the distribution of party tickets and a failure to coordinate properly with BSP Maharashtra state president during state elections. He had been reinstated on the condition that he would not repeat such mistakes and would be assigned responsibility of expanding the party's support base only in other states, not in Uttar Pradesh. ”She also informed that Ashok Siddharth will not be taken back into the party “under any circumstances in the future”.Hardening her stand further against Ashok Siddharth, Mayawati stated that a clear path remains for Akash Anand to resume an active leadership role within the movement, provided Siddharth steps aside completely."In such a situation, keeping in mind the interests of the BSP Party and Movement, as well as his own family and the future of his son-in-law Shri Akash Anand, Shri Ashok Siddharth still has the opportunity to renounce his political ambitions, rise above personal interests, etc., and completely retire from politics. Only then will Shri Akash Anand be able to work freely in the party, and only then will the party sympathetically consider restoring his responsibilities so that he can play an active role in the party—this is the general consensus in the party," Mayawati said in her post.Urging people from the Dalit community, to not engage in any action driven by personal or familial interests that creates obstacles in their path, for which “history may not forgive them," Mayawati cited Ashok Siddharth as a prime example of an official prioritising "personal and familial interests and ambitions over the BSP's mission, despite receiving multiple opportunities to reform."The party gave him not just one but several opportunities to mend his ways, but he prioritised his personal and familial interests and ambitions over the BSP's mission, the consequences of which he himself, along with his son-in-law Shri Akash Anand, has had to bear," Mayawati said in her statement.With the UP assembly elections just months away, a family drama is the last thing that the BSP cadres in the state would have hoped for. The party’s trajectory in the state has been downhill. In the 2022 assembly elections, the BSP could win just 1 seat with a vote share of 12.88%. This was a sharp decline from the 19 seats and a 22.23% vote share that Mayawati had got in 2017.The 2024 Lok Sabha elections went on to showcase that Mayawati’s dismal 2022 performance was not an aberration. The BSP supremo failed to win even one Lok Sabha seat, while her party’s vote share dipped to 9.4% from 19.43% in 2019. Clearly, the results reinforced the gradual decline in BSP’s influence among Dalits.From a sweeping majority in 2007 to allegations of being the B-team of BJP, the BSP’s political fortunes have nosedived in the state. The BSP supporters have dwindled and some have even changed loyalties, but what remains still strong is Mayawati’s appeal and popularity among the party’s cadres.However, the 2027 challenge is going to be tough for Maywati and her BSP. The SP-Congress alliance managed to garner a lot of Dalit support in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, upsetting BJP’s applecart in the state and eventually at the Centre. Cleary this was not the time when the BSP chief should have precipitated action against Akash Anand and pitched one nephew against the other.Mayawati needs a strong comeback and to ensure that she has to first set her house in order. All the more, as she has announced that BSP will not enter into any alliance in future elections. The BSP needs to perform if Mayawati wants to remain relevant in the state’s politics. Another poor show where she wins votes but not seats will reinforce allegations that BSP is the B-team of the BJP.
Article Summary: Mayawati said akash anand, the bsp's national coordinator, would continue to work in the party. Her father-in-law, former rajya sabha mp ashok siddharth, retired from politics and social life. Akash anand entered politics in 2017 at the young age of 22. Mayawati appointed him bsp’s national coordinator in june 2019.

Article Title: Global climate record: August this year joint-warmest month with July '23
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Aug 2026 was the joint-warmest month ever recorded globally across all calendar months, on a par with July 2023, said Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) of the European Union's space programme on Thursday.It noted that this Aug was 1.65° Celsius above the estimated pre-industrial (1850-1900) baseline, marking the first month above 1.5° Celsius since Nov 2025, and the period from June to Aug 2026 was the joint-warmest three-month period on record globally, on a par with 2024."Aug 2026 was a remarkable month in the global climate record. It was both the warmest Aug and the warmest month ever recorded," said Samantha Burgess, strategic lead for climate at European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts. Though the global average temperature rise in the month breached the limit of 1.5°C, it technically did not cross the Paris Agreement threshold, which actually refers to long-term temperature increase over decades, not over one to five years.Under the Paris Agreement, countries agreed to keep long-term global average surface temperature well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels and pursue efforts to limit it to 1.5°C by end of century.Nevertheless, the rise in temperatures to this level in Aug is a stark warning that the world is getting warmer, with its consequences of extreme weather events, glacier melt, sea-level rise and uneven distribution of rainfall over a short period of time being visible across the globe."Until humanity stops burning colossal amount of coal, oil and gas, the pollution this causes will keep baking our planet, and extreme heat will keep smashing all-time records, killing millions and costing trillions, hitting transport and health systems, and pushing up prices for household basics like food," said UN Climate Change executive secretary Simon Stiell in his response to the report.Aug in India was the warmest Aug in the country since 1901, with a mean monthly temperature of 28.01°C.

Article Title: Brics turns 25: How a Goldman Sachs acronym became a global power bloc
Article Text:
New Delhi will play host to the 18th Brics Summit

From a Wall Street acronym to a global grouping

Why Brics matters in the changing global order

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The 18th Brics Summit is set to take place in New Delhi on September 12-13, bringing together leaders of the expanded grouping at a time when wars, trade tensions and a shifting global order are testing its ability to act as a united bloc.India is hosting the summit as the current Brics chair, with the grouping now comprising 11 members and 10 partner countries.Under the theme “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability,” New Delhi has placed greater focus on cooperation across economic and financial issues, technology, energy, development and global governance.The scale of that transformation becomes clearer when traced back to the origins of Brics, a term coined 25 years ago by a Goldman Sachs economist to describe four emerging economies that he believed would become major drivers of global growth.Twenty-five years ago, Brics did not exist as a political grouping. It was a term coined by Goldman Sachs economist Jim O’Neill in 2001 to describe Brazil, Russia, India and China as emerging economies that could become major drivers of global growth.His paper, Building Better Global Economic BRICs, argued that the weight of these economies in the world economy would rise significantly and called for their greater representation in global policymaking forums.The transition from an economic concept to a government-led grouping began in 2006, when the foreign ministers of Brazil, Russia, India and China met on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York. The first summit of their leaders followed in 2009 in Yekaterinburg, Russia, giving the grouping a formal leaders-level platform.The following year, South Africa joined, turning BRIC into Brics and giving the grouping its first member from Africa.The next major transformation came at the 2023 Johannesburg Summit, when Brics agreed to its first large-scale expansion. Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia and the UAE were invited to join from January 1, 2024. Indonesia subsequently became the bloc's 11th full member in January 2025.The expansion also created a partner-country category, allowing a wider group of developing economies to engage with Brics without becoming full members.Brics has evolved from a forum focused largely on economic cooperation into a broader platform for emerging and developing economies seeking a greater role in global governance.Its members have repeatedly called for reforms in institutions such as the United Nations and international financial institutions, arguing that the architecture of global governance should better reflect the changing balance of economic power.Its growing importance is also backed by institutions created by the grouping itself. The New Development Bank, established in 2015, was designed to mobilise resources for infrastructure and sustainable-development projects in Brics and other emerging and developing economies.The bloc's significance has increased further with its expansion. The addition of countries such as Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, the UAE and Indonesia has widened Brics' economic and geographic reach and strengthened its claim to be a platform for the Global South.
Article Summary: The 18th brics summit is set to take place in new delhi on september 12-13. India is hosting the summit as the current brics chair. Brics has evolved from a forum focused largely on economic cooperation into a broader platform for emerging and developing economies seeking a greater role in global governance.

CHANDIGARH: In a major outreach to attract global capital and boost industrial development as envisioned by Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, Punjab Industries and Commerce Minister Aman Arora on Monday met Abdulla Ahmed Al Suwaidi, Secretary General of the UAE International Investment Council (UAEIIC), on the sidelines of the Annual Investment Meeting (AIM) in Dubai to discuss expansive opportunities for mobilising investments into the state.According to the Information and Public Relations Department, Punjab, during the meeting, the Industries Minister discussed Punjab’s vast economic potential with Abdulla Ahmed Al Suwaidi and invited UAE investors to tap into high-growth sectors through government, semi-government and private sector partnerships.Reiterating the state government’s resolve, Arora assured the UAEIIC of complete administrative support, handholding and logistical facilitation from the Punjab Government for global enterprises seeking to set up or expand operations in the state. He emphasised that under the visionary leadership of Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, Punjab is keen to build long-term, mutually beneficial partnerships with UAE-based investors and institutional funds.Highlighting the state’s investor-centric reforms, the Minister underscored the ease of doing business facilitated through ‘Invest Punjab’—the state’s unified single-window platform that delivers prompt statutory approvals and clearances to ensure a smooth, hassle-free investment journey.“Punjab offers a highly conducive entrepreneurial ecosystem, excellent multimodal connectivity, skilled technical manpower, and a transparent governance framework. We invite UAE business leaders to become active partners in Punjab’s transformative economic growth story,” Arora said.The UAE UAEIIC, which unites the UAE’s public and private entities to channel outward foreign direct investment (FDI), welcomed the state delegation's proactive outreach. The engagement focused on establishing robust institutional linkages to enable direct capital inflows and joint ventures between the UAE and Punjab, the Public Relations Department said.Expressing confidence in the discussions, Arora noted that this engagement marks a significant milestone that will pave the way for deeper bilateral economic cooperation, stronger business ties and substantial investment pipelines in Punjab.
Article Summary: Punjab industries and commerce minister aman arora met abdulla ahmed al suwaidi, secretary general of the uae international investment council (uaeiic) the two discussed expansive opportunities for mobilising investments into the state. Arora assured the uaeiic of complete administrative support, handholding and logistical facilitation from the punjab government.

Article Title: Strategic Autonomy in motion as India hosts 18th BRICS Summit
Article Text:
This would be the 18th summit of the grouping. (Photo: ANI)

India for BRICS

Key Challenges for India

India will host the annual BRICS summit on September 12-13 at Bharat Mandapam, returning to the venue where it held the G20 summit in 2023. That gathering is remembered for the inclusion of the African Union in G20, marking a major step in efforts to bridge the gap between the Western-led global order and the emerging Global South. At BRICS, India will look to leverage that momentum, working with major emerging economies to demand structural reforms of global governance institutions dominated by the West.This would be the 18th summit of the grouping that brings together 11 major emerging and developing economies – Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, Ethiopia, UAE, Indonesia, Iran, Egypt and Saudi Arabia – along with 10 other partner countries. Together, BRICS nations account for 49 percent of world population, 40 percent of global GDP and 26 percent of international trade.The last time India hosted an in-person BRICS summit was in 2016 in Goa. This year also marks 2 decades of formalisation of the bloc for cooperation on issues related to global economic and political governance. The theme of India's 2026 chairship is Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability, drawing inspiration from PM Narendra Modi's 'humanity first' and people-centric approach to BRICS.This will also be the first summit to see in-person participation by Russian President Vladimir Putin since the start of the Ukraine war. Chinese President Xi Jinping is also visiting India for the first time in 7 years to participate in the summit.Under its chairship, India has so far held over 350 meetings - 25 at the ministerial level including the foreign ministers and national security advisers’ engagements. The ministerial meetings have so far resulted in key outcomes and initiatives spanning agriculture, health, energy, environment, disaster management and also trade, reaffirming commitment to a fair, inclusive and transparent multilateral trading system with WTO at its core.Despite the political fragmentation and economic imbalances associated with the grouping, BRICS remains important for India for multiple reasons, especially in an increasingly uncertain world. For one, it lends India a platform to practice its strategic autonomy and multi-alignment policy, not allowing any one single bloc to acquire excessive leverage over it. That it can simultaneously expand its strategic and technology ties with the West and also work with Quad for a free and open Indo-Pacific reinforces an independent foreign policy. For India, as external affairs minister S Jaishankar has said, BRICS is an embodiment of a multipolar world. India is not giving up on its Western partnerships, only hedging against uncertainty whether from US unpredictability or Chinese ascendancy.BRICS also allows India to showcase its Global South leadership credentials, as it works with other major emerging markets to push for reforms of global institutions like the UNSC, IMF and World Bank that are not representative of the developing world. Support for UNSC reforms is important, although it still falls short of an explicit endorsement of India's permanent membership bid, mainly because of China's presence.India's approach to BRICS is also guided by its complex ties with China. Turning away would mean allowing China to single-handedly shape the agenda of the developing world. BRICS is consensus driven and even for Washington and other Western capitals, India's moderating influence should be of significance as it prevents the bloc from turning into an anti-West platform.There's focus as well on expanding financial architecture as no government would like its trade to be held hostage by instruments it can't control. As Jaishankar has underlined, institutions such as the New Development Bank and the Contingent Reserve Arrangement demonstrate the group's ability to create credible alternatives. For India, these are not initiatives targeted at any currency. In any case, India has officially said it's against de-dollarisation or any attempt to target the US currency. It has also ruled out any proposal for a common BRICS currency.BRICS provides India with markets, along with trade diversification, de-risking and supply-chain opportunities. According to a commerce ministry press release, intra-BRICS merchandise trade reached approximately $1.17 trillion in 2024. India exported an estimated $82 billion in goods to BRICS members in FY2025–26, alongside approximately $31.3 billion in services exports in 2024. BRICS membership deepens India’s trade relationships with Russia (energy), Brazil (agriculture/commodities), Gulf and African countries, diversifying away from overreliance on any single partner.The first of course is to forge a consensus on West Asia that would enable a joint BRICS declaration, a task complicated by the presence of the UAE and Iran in the group. India would not like the event to end with a Chair's Statement, like what happened with the foreign ministers' meeting, knowing well that no BRICS summit has concluded without a comprehensive joint declaration. Foreign secretary Vikram Misri said last week India has received cooperation from all members and the government is working to arrive eventually at a constructive outcome that benefits all BRICS stakeholders. India will focus on drafting a resolution rooted in the UN Charter, dialogue and diplomacy, freedom of navigation and civilian protection, while looking to ringfence economic agreements from contentious political issues by acknowledging respective national positions.Balancing relations with the US is another key concern for India, which is hosting the summit fresh off a tariff firestorm with Washington. US President Donald Trump sees the grouping itself as an assault on the US currency and has threatened to impose 100 percent tariffs on BRICS nations if they work to replace the US dollar. India backs legitimate local-currency settlement, while maintaining it is against any common BRICS currency or China-centered replacement mechanism. As it walks the diplomatic tightrope, India must steer initiatives like the integration of central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) but without appearing to endorse any anti-dollar bloc.Another challenge for India is to prevent China's predominance without destabilising its bilateral relations with Beijing. For all the talk about BRICS' combined power, China enjoys a vastly asymmetrical influence with its trade, investment, manufacturing and critical mineral leverage. Wary of China's efforts to advance its own economic interests, India has not endorsed SCO’s 2030 economic roadmap and it must find a way to work with China in BRICS on shared objectives but without allowing the forum to be co-opted as a Chinese economic or geopolitical platform.This also intersects with the challenge of ensuring that an expanded grouping remains governable and cohesive, especially with countries like Pakistan and Bangladesh pursuing membership with support from Beijing. True multipolarity and consensus-driven equality within the organisation are key imperatives for India.As Jaishankar said while announcing India's summit agenda, BRICS must transition now from a forum for discussions to a platform for delivery. In that spirit, India seems focused on delivering an outcome-oriented summit with key deliverables like a unanimous BRICS declaration, logistics supply-chain cooperation framework, incubator/ startup network, development finance, cross-border payment and continued support for Indian priorities like UNSC reforms and counterterrorism.To conclude, inclusion of the African Union was not the only major takeaway from the G20 summit in 2023. Perhaps more dramatic was the last-minute consensus on Ukraine through a compromise language crafted by India, allowing a G20 declaration. India can take confidence from that diplomatic triumph, heading into another tough but potentially rewarding global summit.
Article Summary: India will host the annual brics summit on september 12-13 at bharat mandapam. The theme of india's 2026 chairship is building for resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability. This would be the 18th summit of the grouping that brings together 11 major emerging and developing economies.

Article Title: Former NFL star LeShon Johnson sentenced to five years in prison over massive dogfighting ring
Article Text:
LeShon Johnson receives five-year prison sentence in dogfighting case

Former NFL player LeShon Johnson could appeal sentence

Former NFL running back LeShon Johnson has been sentenced to five years in federal prison after being convicted in connection with a large-scale dogfighting operation in Oklahoma. The case has drawn renewed attention to his life after football, with prosecutors describing a long-running operation that caused the deaths and serious injuries of hundreds of dogs.Johnson, 55, received his sentence Thursday in an Oklahoma federal court. Along with five years behind bars, he was ordered to serve three years of supervised release and pay a $30,000 fine.The former running back surrendered 190 dogs to the government following his conviction. According to the Department of Justice, that was the largest number of dogs seized from a single person in a federal dogfighting case.Federal prosecutors linked Johnson to Mal Kant Kennels, an Oklahoma operation that had been breeding and trafficking pit bulls since at least 2007. Investigators said the dogs were bred for fighting traits and that Johnson promoted bloodlines connected to successful fighting dogs.The case is especially serious because this was not Johnson's first encounter with dogfighting charges. He pleaded guilty to state dogfighting charges in 2004 and received a five-year deferred sentence, according to court records.His latest conviction involved six felony counts tied to possessing, selling, transporting and delivering dogs for use in animal fighting.Associate Attorney General Stanley E. Woodward Jr. strongly condemned the operation after the sentence was announced."LeShon Johnson will face justice for building another particularly egregious and violent dog fighting scheme," associate attorney general Stanley E. Woodward Jr. said in a statement Thursday. "As Johnson was well aware, dog fighting is a felony in all 50 states. To anyone attempting to build violent and illicit business schemes: you can run, but you can't hide from the Department of Justice."Johnson's legal team had pushed for a much lighter punishment. His attorney, Billy Coyle IV, asked the court to consider probation and pointed to Johnson's medical condition, his lack of recent criminal history and the fact that he had remained on pretrial release for more than two years without violations.Coyle also argued that Johnson had serious health problems and had experienced multiple concussions and traumatic brain injuries during his football career. Court documents said he had required a daily caretaker for the past two years."The main point was just to show the court that he'd been out on bond for pretrial release for over two years," Coyle said. "He's got no infractions whatsoever. He doesn't drink. He doesn't smoke. I don't think the necessity of sending him to prison or jail was necessary."Coyle later said he was surprised by the five-year sentence and expected to recommend an appeal, although Johnson had not made a final decision.Prosecutors had sought a 10-year sentence, arguing that Johnson played a leadership role in the operation. They also pointed to the deaths and injuries involving hundreds of dogs as a reason against reducing his punishment.Johnson's football career once put him in the national spotlight. He played for the Green Bay Packers, Arizona Cardinals and New York Giants between 1994 and 1999 before later playing in the XFL. At Northern Illinois, he earned unanimous All-American honors in 1993 and finished sixth in Heisman Trophy voting.His federal sentence now marks a stark and troubling chapter in the former NFL player's post-football life.
Article Summary: Leshon johnson receives five-year prison sentence in dogfighting case. Former nfl player could appeal sentence. Prosecutors describe a long-running operation that caused the deaths and serious injuries of hundreds of dogs. The former running back surrendered 190 dogs to the government following his conviction.
